options: A. haven’t found the mutant gene yet.
B. haven’t been able to study the mutant gene on its own yet.
C. haven’t been able to confirm the results of their tests yet.

questions.explanation: S1: Yeah, but until we isolate it, testing cannot commence so the whole project is on hold at the moment. (This matches B).

questions.instruction_text: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

options: B. ahead of schedule but making slow progress now.
C. in a six-month testing phase.

questions.explanation: L: After all, correct me if I'm wrong, but did we not say a timeframe of maybe six months just to identify the culprit? S1: Yes, but having done that so quickly in the space of a week, it's frustrating to have to wait now. (This matches B).

questions.instruction_text: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

question_data.text: 29 The infection associated with the mutant gene
options: A. is passed directly from parent to child.
C. cannot be passed on to the next or subsequent generation.

questions.explanation: S2: We have managed to establish that the gene mutation bypasses every other generation... If the parent is infected, the child will be a silent carrier, who will go on to infect any children he or she has. (This matches B).

questions.instruction_text: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

options: A. Bird Flu may cure the mutant-gene infection.
B. a symptom of Bird Flu may be key to fighting the mutant-gene infection.
C. a low body temperature may cure the mutant-gene infection.

questions.explanation: S3: We don't think it was the virus, but the accompanying fever. His body temperature was raised to 105. We have a hypothesis that the mutant gene couldn't cope with such an excessive internal body temperature. (Fever is a symptom, matches B).

question_data.text: First find a suitable dig site by surface-collecting - aim to locate a midden (place where 31 [blank] used to be dumped).
question_data.word_limit_text: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS

questions.explanation: Lecturer: Ideally, you'll look to find a 'midden'; that is m-i-d-d-e-n. an archaic term for a refuse site... people would simply dig a random hole and designate it as the spot to throw rubbish in, and that's your 'midden'.
